evals.name: phase-discipline
evals.expected_output: Implements 4 phases sequentially, running make test after each phase. Phase 2 depends on Phase 1, Phase 3 depends on Phase 2. Agent should test after each phase and fix issues before proceeding.

assertions.text: make test is executed at least 3 times across the transcript (after separate phases, not just once at the end)
Phase 1 (remove_item) is implemented and verified before Phase 2 (total_value) begins
Phase 2 (total_value) is implemented and verified before Phase 3 (apply_discount) begins
Checkboxes in the plan file are marked progressively as phases complete, not all at once at the end
inventory.py contains remove_item, total_value, and apply_discount methods
make test exits 0 with all tests passing
Plan file has all checkboxes marked [x]

evals.name: ambiguous-mismatch
evals.expected_output: Detects naming mismatches: plan references 'Order' (actual: PurchaseOrder), 'compute_total(tax_percent)' (actual: calculate_total(tax_rate, discount_code)), 'cancel(note)' (actual tests: 'reason'). These are naming mismatches — agent should adapt to actual names, document deviations in the plan, and continue without pausing.

assertions.text: Detects that the plan references 'Order' class but the actual class is 'PurchaseOrder'
Detects that the plan references 'compute_total(tax_percent)' but the actual method is 'calculate_total(tax_rate, discount_code)'
Detects that the plan uses 'cancel(note)' / 'self.cancel_note' but the tests expect 'cancel(reason)' / 'self.cancellation_reason'
Adapts to actual codebase names (uses PurchaseOrder, cancel(reason), cancellation_reason) rather than creating new classes or renaming existing ones
Documents naming deviations as inline notes in the plan file
Does NOT rename PurchaseOrder to Order or create a new Order class
cancel and status_history are correctly added to PurchaseOrder and all tests pass

evals.name: manual-verification
evals.expected_output: Implements Phase 1 (center_text) without pausing. After Phase 2 (format_table), pauses and presents the Manual Verification items for user confirmation. Does NOT auto-check the manual verification checkboxes.

assertions.text: Phase 1 (center_text) is completed and agent proceeds to Phase 2 without pausing for user input
After Phase 2 (format_table), agent pauses and presents the Manual Verification items to the user
Pause message lists the specific manual verification items from the plan (visual alignment, dash separators, column widths)
Manual Verification checkboxes are NOT marked [x] by the agent — they remain [ ] for user confirmation
formatter.py contains both center_text and format_table functions
make test exits 0 with all tests passing
Phase 1 and Phase 2 code checkboxes are marked [x]

evals.name: cascade-dependencies
evals.expected_output: Implements 5 phases in strict order (Task model → TaskRepository → TaskService → integration → CLI helper). Each phase builds on the previous. Phase 3 has a subtle note about get_summary counting that requires attention. All implemented in tracker.py.

assertions.text: Phase 1 (Task model) is implemented before Phase 2 (TaskRepository)
Phase 2 (TaskRepository) is implemented before Phase 3 (TaskService)
make test is executed after each phase (at least 4 times across transcript)
Checkboxes are marked progressively as each phase completes
tracker.py contains Task, TaskRepository, TaskService classes and format_task_list function
TaskService.get_summary correctly returns total reflecting current repo count (accounts for deletions)
make test exits 0 with all tests passing
Plan file has all checkboxes marked [x]
Any deviations from the plan are noted in the plan file or communicated to the user

evals.name: evolved-codebase
evals.expected_output: Detects that string_helpers.py does not exist — the code has been split into text_utils.py (slugify, word_count) and text_transforms.py (truncate, title_case). The plan's assumptions about file structure are wrong. Agent should report these mismatches before implementing.

assertions.text: Detects that string_helpers.py does not exist
Identifies that the codebase has text_utils.py and text_transforms.py instead
Detects that functions are split across two files (slugify/word_count in text_utils, truncate/title_case in text_transforms)
Presents the file structure mismatch before starting implementation
Uses structured Issue/Expected/Found format to communicate the mismatch
If agent adapts, new functions are added to the correct existing files (contains_any/extract_emails to text_utils.py, pad_right/pad_center/repeat_text to text_transforms.py)
Does NOT create a new string_helpers.py file
If agent proceeds, make test exits 0 with all tests passing

evals.name: resume-buggy-phase
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 is marked [x] but validate_age has a bug: uses >= 120 instead of > 120, so age 120 is rejected. The agent should start with Phase 2 (trusting checkmarks), but when running tests, discover that test_validate_age_boundary_120 fails. It should investigate and identify the Phase 1 bug.

assertions.text: Agent starts implementation from Phase 2 (respects Phase 1 [x] checkmarks)
Agent implements the register function in Phase 2
When tests fail, agent investigates rather than only modifying Phase 2 code
Agent identifies that the bug is in validate_age (Phase 1): >= 120 should be > 120
Agent communicates that a previously-completed phase has a bug before fixing it
The bug is fixed: validate_age correctly accepts age 120
registration.py contains register and batch_register functions
make test exits 0 with all tests passing
